summary: IDS feed s065_single is degraded due to high encrypted traffic share (68.9% vs 60% IDS tolerance). All other checks (duplicates, VLANs, directionality, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 68.9% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/HTTPS), exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is forwarded without broker-side decryption, so payload remains opaque to the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection. With ~69% encrypted bytes, the IDS cannot inspect payload content, creating a blind spot for malware, C2, and exploits carried inside TLS and reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Selective TLS decryption/visibility at the packet broker (or via dedicated SSL visibility appliance) will provide a decrypted copy to the IDS while respecting privacy policy, bringing encrypted share below 60% and restoring payload inspection capability.
